title: Interpretable Singing Emotion Recognition Using Acoustic and Vocal Technique Features
abstract_en: Singing emotion recognition relies predominantly on deep learning models that achieve strong performance but offer limited insight into the vocal characteristics driving emotion, of- ten overlooking the singing voice as a distinct signal. We propose an interpretable singing emotion recognition framework using a compact set of singing-specific descriptors across prosody, spec- tral features, phonetics, and vocal technique. To decode model decisions and link predictions to measurable acoustic phenomena, we employ SHAP and apply GRAD-CAM to qualitatively assess the learned representations of vocal techniques. Evaluations show that singing-specific features reduce cross-singer variability, while vocal technique descriptors provide interpretable insights into singing expression. Furthermore, out-of-domain evaluation on VocalSet reveals interesting associations between emotional expression and ground-truth technical execution. The analysis highlights vibrato and pharyngeal techniques as salient cues of emotional delivery, with SHAP indicating that vibrato is context-dependent on articulation rate. These findings emphasize the value of domain-specific features for interpretable singing emotion analysis.

title: Acquisition for Spherical-Linear Bayesian Optimization on the Cube
abstract_en: Recent work demonstrated that executing Bayesian Optimization (BO) using simply a linear surrogate with a clever transformation is enough to approximate the performance of the standard Gaussian-Process (GP) based version on high-dimensional test functions. When the decision region is a sphere, this strategy admits rapid exact acquisition. However, it is the unit cube we encounter most often in the BO literature, and in this setting a standard approach, namely a multi-start quasi-Newton method, is employed for solving the acquisition subproblem. In this article, we will discuss a series of results, both positive and negative, regarding the complexity of global resolution of various acquisition subproblems over the unit cube. On the basis of this discussion, we will propose a new acquisition function which is globally optimizable using significantly less execution time than the incumbent approach while maintaining or improving performance. The resulting method is competitive with GP-based BO in terms of accuracy per evaluation, and is superior in terms of accuracy per walltime on black-boxes of low to moderate computational intensity.

title: LGMT: A Tool for Testing the Logical Reasoning Reliability of LLMs
abstract_en: Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly serve as reasoning components in modern software systems, yet a model that answers a logical query correctly can contradict itself when the same problem is restated in an equivalent form. Static benchmarks evaluate queries in isolation and therefore fail to expose such inconsistencies. To address this limitation, we present LGMT, an open-source tool that detects reasoning inconsistencies through metamorphic relations grounded in first-order logic. Given a source test case in premise-conclusion form, LGMT generates logically equivalent follow-up cases and checks whether the model's entailment predictions agree across the pair, without ground-truth labels. The tool provides 20 built-in metamorphic relations, supports custom ones verified by the Z3 theorem prover, and runs from a CLI or a web studio, including an offline mock mode requiring no API key. Across six widely used LLMs on a bundled benchmark of 3,091 metamorphic groups, LGMT reveals inconsistency rates ranging from 20.84% to 29.44%. LGMT is publicly available on GitHub at https://github.com/MaxwelsDonc/lgmt-tool, with a demonstration video at https://youtu.be/gou4opptu1U.

title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Loss Exploration for Vision-Based Perception under Non-IID Data
abstract_en: Vision-based image classification models benefit from Federated Learning (FL) across vehicles, however learning accurate models from distributed vehicular cameras is challenging due to data heterogeneity and privacy concerns. To improve performance on non-IID data, advanced FL optimization approaches have emerged that share auxiliary insights, such as client gradient behaviors. While these gradient-guided optimized FL methods improve the model accuracy, their reliance on sharing additional gradient information introduces a previously unexplored privacy vulnerability. In our empirical privacy-leakage experiment, we show that a malicious server can infer clients' label sets from shared guidance matrices under heterogeneous client label distributions (simulated via Dirichlet-based label partitions), between 50% and 84% accuracy. To address this privacy leakage, we propose PPFLex that replaces the central server with three Secure Multi-Party Computation (MPC) servers to securely compute the global guidance matrix and perform federated averaging under semi-honest and malicious MPC server assumptions. We evaluate PPFLex on widely used traffic-sign classification datasets (e.g., GTSRB and BTSC) as representative autonomous vehicle perception benchmarks, comparing against baselines. Our results show that PPFLex achieves accuracy comparable to the plain-text FedLEx pipeline while preventing privacy leakage, incurring acceptable MPC overhead.

title: Energy Discontinuity of the Lyapunov Exponent for Quasiperiodic Schrödinger Operators with Gevrey Potentials
abstract_en: We construct quasiperiodic Schrödinger operators with Gevrey potentials for which the Lyapunov exponent is discontinuous in the spectral energy. More precisely, let \(α\in\R\setminus\mathbb Q\) satisfy the Diophantine condition \(\|kα\|_{\T}\geqγ|k|^{-τ}\) for all \(k\in\Z\setminus\{0\}\), with \(γ>0\) and \(τ\geq1\). For every Gevrey index \(\mathfrak s>1+τ\) and every sufficiently large coupling \(λ\), we construct a real-valued potential \(v_λ\in G^{\mathfrak s}(\T,\R)\) and a sequence of energies \(E_j\downarrow0\) such that \[ L_{v_λ}(0)\geq(1-\varepsilon_λ)\logλ, \qquad \sup_{j\geq1} L_{v_λ}(E_j)\leq(1-c_*)\logλ, \] where \(L_{v_λ}(E)\) denotes the Lyapunov exponent of the Schrödinger operator with potential \(λv_λ\), \(c_*>0\) is an absolute constant, and \(\varepsilon_λ\to0\) as \(λ\to\infty\). For bounded-type frequencies (\(τ=1\)), the regularity range \(\mathfrak s>2\) is sharp up to the endpoint \(\mathfrak s=2\), since the Lyapunov exponent is known to be continuous in energy for \(1<\mathfrak s<2\).
